questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I chose Berlin mainly because of the cultural life and opportunities. I was also interested in the language, and the German universities offer excellent language courses for international students, both a "Vorkurs" before the semester begins (with a fee) and classes during the semester (for free)!

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I had the time of my life and really encourage my fellow students to do a semester at Freie Universität Berlin (FU) if they feel like it. You won't regret it, this city has so much to offer.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I found it quite easy. In the months leading up to my departure, I received multiple e-mails from FU with important information which I read thoroughly, so I wasn't worried about all the practical stuff upon arrival. But beware that much of the information you receive is in German. If you know a little German and have some patience though, you will be fine. I also found the international coordinators really helpful. They held an online introduction meeting for international students a few weeks before the semester began.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: International students were offered an introductory tour on campus by some of the student coordinators. There you were able to ask questions and most importantly: get all the pro tips from a student who already knows how the bureaucracy, online portalts etc. work.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: I felt completely safe, and the erasmus/international office were super willing to help when I was in doubt of something.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
Finding housing is challenging!! I initially tried to find housing through WG gesucht which people I know personally as well as older KU student reports had suggested. This was not a succes, a lot of work and no results. I was lucky to find something relatively cheap on AirBnb, 6400 for a 30 m2 room that I shared with my partner, so 3200 each.
When I got here and met young Berliners, I found out that finding housing has become a huge problem over the past years. The best tip is you use your network if you have any in Berlin. Reach out to people you know that lived or studied in Berlin, maybe they can put you in contact with a former roomate, friends etc. Reach out on the group "dansker i Berlin" on Facebook. Begin looking at least 3 months before your stay. Use official rental companies like AirBnb etc. And look out for scams!!

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: You might have a bit more transport time to the uni that you're used to, but in my opinion, it is totally worth it. Everything that is interesting in Berlin is located closer to the center than the housing offered by FU.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: My fellow students that live in the student housing offered by FU seem satisfied with the facilities, so it's not a totally shitty option, but in my opinion they are located WAY too far away from everything (in the most southern part of the city...). I definitely prefer living closer to the center where all the interesting stuff in the city actually happens.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Campus management can be a bit tricky because it works differently than the KU system. Be patient and make sure to read all the material that you are sent before your arrival, and there will actually be guides for everything (you will freaking love how thorough Germans are)

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You sign up in the system called Campus Management (guides for both campus management as well as the two other online systems ZEDAT and Blackboard will be sent to you by e-mail!). The registration is opened up on a certain date a few weeks before the semester begins. You sign up for the classes that you want, and a few weeks later you find out whether you got them or not. The cool thing is that (in contrary to KU) you are allowed to try out the classes for a few weeks after signing up, and if you changed your mind, you can cancel your registration and choose another class. So convenient

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The erasmus office at FU can explain everything, reach out to them by e-mail or go to their office

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Got all of them

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Don't stress too much about it, exchange is about so many other things, and if you fuck it up the erasmus office at FU can help you

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Excellent. I loved my professors

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: MA level

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The teaching style was super inclusive, and my professors had a lot of enthusiasm. That's the most striking difference. I can't remember the last time one of my KU professors didn't seem tired of life and academia and cuts

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
1: Language course, German A2-B1
2: Decolonizing Classrooms, Psychological Anthropology

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Ultimativt fedeste by at bo i i forhold til kulturliv, klubber, musik, kunst, you name it. Der er masser af sportsmuligheder på universitetet, tjek deres klub (får man også mailinfo om)

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Der er ikke rigtig fester som på KU, men der er til gengæld mange flere muligheder ude i byen. Der er en international klub på uni med sociale arrangementer, men har ikke udforsket den.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Der er både mulighed for at deltage i universitetets tilbud, men der er også mange andre muligheder ude i byen, alt efter hvor dine interesser ligger. Jeg er engageret i politik derhjemme, så det var nemt for mig at finde et netværk hernede ved at opsøge politiske grupper. Virkelig oplagt måde at få et lokalt netværk, for ellers er det mest udvekslingsstuderende, man møder (hvilket uden tvivl også er super fedt)

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Hvis du er til musik og natteliv, så tjek events på Resident Advisor, og du vil aldrig løbe tør for noget at lave i weekenden. Når det er varmt, så tag i de udendørs sommerbade eller tag til en af strandene

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Ja, meget lig DK

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Som nævnt, hvis du har en hobby derhjemme, så er det oplagt at dyrke den her i en lokal klub/organisation/netværk

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Ikke rigtig

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Åbenhed over for forskellighed

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1: Semesterstrukturen er anderledes end i andre europæiske lande, så det kan være en udfordring: 1. april-30. september (sommersemester) og 1. oktober-31. marts (vintersemester). Det er dog ikke umuligt at få til at gå op med studierne derhjemme, og for mig er det i hvert fald klart alt besværet værd:)
2: Det siger sig selv, at sommersemesteret er sjovere end den mørke vinter, så sørg for at søge det hvis muligt.
3: Just do it, Berlin er seriøst det fedeste sted at bo
